title: Joe Oliver and the rivalry of the dozens
summary: Oliver worked the next corner, and the two traded insults and played the dozens.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: Oh yeah. Yeah, because Mr. Groeschel, he was determined because I'm working at one corner, and he's at Pete Lawless at the next corner. See? And Joe, they'd all pass and kick one another at night. If he'd see my boss out there, he'd tell him, say, you better get a band in there, I'd say, cut that fella out there. He can't see, he can't play, he can't blow, nothing. You know, talk about him, kick one another. Yeah, yeah. Now he's got one eye himself, he cock-eyed himself, see? But yet and still, he was just a fella that liked to play the dozens, you know, talk about you.
That's not heard there. He used to kid everybody a lot.
